title: Recibry
description: Recibry is a personal recipe library app built with React, Next.js, CSS, and Tailwind, designed to solve the common problem of recipes scattered across notes, screenshots, and bookmarked sites. The Library page gives users a single, account-based home for their collection, with a clean, minimal interface built around Tailwind's utility-first styling and Next.js handling routing and server-side rendering for fast, responsive performance across devices.

Each saved recipe supports photos, personal ratings, and private cooking notes, letting users build a genuinely personal cookbook rather than a generic list. A standout feature is PDF export, so any recipe can be pulled offline or printed for use in the kitchen. Combined with authenticated sign-in for individual libraries, Recibry demonstrates full-stack thinking around user data, content organization, and a practical, everyday use case.

title: EQC Resource Hub
description: EQC Resource Hub is a centralised resource management platform built for trainers at the RTO I work for, solving the common problem of trainers going into class unprepared because resources are scattered across personal computers, messily renamed cloud folders, or missing entirely. Built with EJS, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript on a MongoDB backend, the hub is managed by college admins, who upload trainer-created resources along with an overview, recommended usage, screenshots, and how-to videos. Resources are categorised into six types and linked to subjects and courses, so trainers can browse or search by keyword to find what they need.

Instead of blindly downloading files like a shared drive, trainers open a resource viewer page to read the overview, watch videos, and check screenshots before downloading, along with who uploaded it and when. Role-based access control limits trainers to viewing and downloading while admins retain full control, and the UI uses SortableJS for drag-and-drop organisation. The hub is now used daily by around 60 trainers at the college.

title: Salon Diadem
description: Salon Diadem is a boutique hair salon in Eglinton, Western Australia, and the site was built with Svelte, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Bootstrap to match the salon's luxe, minimalist branding. The layout leans on clean typography, generous whitespace, and full-bleed lifestyle photography to carry the brand story across the home, services, about, and contact pages, all fully responsive across desktop, tablet, and mobile.

The services section breaks down the salon's colour work, precision cuts, restorative treatments, nanoplasty, and packages, with each entry linking straight through to the salon's Phorest booking platform so enquiries convert into appointments without friction. Supporting sections such as client testimonials, trading hours, and the Sustainable Salons certification badge build trust, making this a polished, production-ready site that gives a small local business a genuinely premium online presence.

title: "Ryan's Space" Online Portfolio
description: My personal portfolio website, ryancjeffrey.com, was built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Node.js and Express.js handling the backend routing of static pages. The site is deployed via Vercel, with CI/CD pipelines integrated through GitHub, ensuring that updates pushed to the repository are automatically deployed with minimal friction.

This setup not only improves development efficiency but also demonstrates my familiarity with modern DevOps workflows. The site showcases both my technical skills and design sensibilities, providing a clean, responsive user experience while serving as a central hub for my professional projects and experience.

title: Project Pricing Calculators
description: The pricing calculator was built using HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript, providing a fast, lightweight, and responsive user experience without the overhead of additional libraries or frameworks. I chose this tech stack to ensure the tool would load quickly, work across all modern browsers, and remain easy to maintain and customize.

JavaScript handles the dynamic calculations and input validation, while CSS was used to create a clean, intuitive user interface that aligns with the overall branding of 3 Yellow Circles. This project demonstrates my ability to build interactive, front-end tools that deliver real value to users without relying on external dependencies.

title: 3 Yellow Circles
description: This is the official website for 3 Yellow Circles, built to attract and onboard clients quickly and easily. Developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Express.js, the site lets visitors book a discovery call or get started instantly via a simple form.

It's fully responsive, ensuring a smooth experience on any device, and includes essential pages like services, reviews, about, and contact. This project highlights a clean, user-focused design that supports business growth through accessible, mobile-friendly web development.

title: SWM Cabling Services
description: The SWM Cabling Services website is a full-stack build using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Bootstrap, and Express.js. It delivers a clean, modern layout that highlights key cabling and networking services with simple navigation and clear service sections. The design is fully responsive, providing consistent performance across desktop and mobile.

The backend uses Express.js with SMTP integration to securely process contact form enquiries. Server-side validation and organised routing ensure reliable form delivery and smooth operation. The result is a polished, production-ready site that gives SWM Cabling Services a professional online presence.

title: Tyler Black Concreting
description: The Tyler Black Concreting website is a full-stack project built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Express.js. It features a responsive, professional layout with clear navigation, highlighting services, completed projects, client reviews, and easy contact options. The design adapts seamlessly across desktop and mobile devices for a smooth user experience.

The backend includes SMTP integration to securely handle contact form submissions and deliver inquiries directly to the client's inbox. Server-side routing and form validation ensure reliable operation, making the site a polished, production-ready solution for a small business online presence.

title: Full Stack Task Management Application
description: Here is a full-stack web application developed with the MEN stack. This To Do App is a full-stack web application with a frontend built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and a backend powered by Node.js, Express.js, and MongoDB. It incorporates RESTful APIs for seamless data interaction between the client and server, enabling real-time updates and efficient data management.

Designed with scalability in mind, this application provides a user-friendly interface and a robust backend architecture, demonstrating expertise in frontend, backend, and API integration to deliver a high-performance, dynamic web experience.

title: BMI Calculator
description: This project is a single-document web application built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

Although it is a simple, front-end-only project, it effectively demonstrates the power of the three core web development languages. I frequently use this project as a teaching tool to introduce my web development students to JavaScript fundamentals, including variables and basic interactivity.
